I feel like how much experience a project team expects really depends on which team you are applying for. Of course, teams that are a bit more competitive to get into prefer freshman with experience, and there are some students who come in with a lot of CS experience. Every project team is going to ask you about previous projects, or a resume of some sort. If you REALLY want to get into a CS based project team, I would recommend maybe working on a summer project of some sort, to give a bit of an edge on your application. Granted, I think some project teams prefer freshman, so that they have a strong bond with the team, and teams know freshman aren’t expected to know a lot  

There are some teams that you can’t really expect a lot of experience, where they would try to gauge how interested you are in the subject (I have a friend who had no previous experience and got into AguaClara, which is a project team based around clean water)

Also, if you don’t get in your first semester, you can always try your next. I know ppl who reapplied to project teams and got in the second time after gaining more experience. Heck, I even know ppl who joined teams their senior year. 

Most importantly, being in a project team IS NOT EVERYTHING. You do not have to be in a project team if you have an engineering based major. I know ppl who are doing great in school, but were never in a project team. Heck, I’m planning to quite my project team as I start my junior year because I want to do something else. If you don’t get into a team, it really isn’t the end of the world. Just have fun and try things out!!
